# Hard-to-vary report: Bostrom, "Are You Living in a Computer Simulation?"

## 1. The question, frozen

The paper answers several questions. I froze the one its abstract makes central: **at least one of three propositions is true — (1) almost no civilizations reach a posthuman stage; (2) almost no posthumans want to run ancestor-simulations; (3) almost all observers like us are simulated.** Range: human-level civilizations anywhere, any era, through their whole future. What is asked: which horn must be so, given that posthuman computing power would be vast.

This is not the title's question. The title asks a yes/no, and the paper does not answer it — it ends by splitting credence roughly evenly across the three horns. Saying that plainly is itself a finding: the title promises an answer the argument does not give.

## 2. The explanation in parts

P1 substrate-independence (weak form: replicating brain computation structurally suffices for experience); P2 the numbers (10^42 ops/s planetary computer, 10^14–10^17 per brain, 10^33–36 per human history); P3 N = fI·NI; P4 the ratio fsim = fP·fI·NI/(fP·fI·NI + 1); P5 "NI is extremely large"; P6 the bland indifference principle, credence = fsim; P7 the betting argument; P8 the continuum argument; P9 the convergence speculations; P10 the DOOM/"we are not special" move; P11 the mildness claim and the theogony.

Jobs: J1 make (3) live; J2 leave (1) and (2) live; J3 set credence (author's, §V); J4 survive Bertrand and the Doomsday worry (author's); J5 say what would move our credence (added by me — the paper supplies it, so it is *held if* J5 is real).

## 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| P1 substrate-independence | Borrowed | Rests on philosophy of mind, "taken as given". But the paper swaps strong functionalism for the weak version and the argument still runs: the strong version was loose. That is a genuine tightening. |
| P2 the numbers | Held | Not the numbers — those are loose. Swap 10^42 for 10^30 and nothing breaks. What is held is the inequality: "posthuman computing vastly exceeds the cost of one human history." Rename the part to that. |
| P3, P4 decomposition and ratio | Held | Remove and J1 goes. |
| H, the count of pre-posthuman individuals | Held | Remove H and the ratio is 1 for any N: horns (1) and (2) stop being live, so J2 goes. Small part, real work. |
| P5 "NI extremely large" | Held if | Held by P2 plus "posthumans build many computers". Notably it does *not* need their motives — those are fI. Clean separation. |
| P6 indifference principle | Held if | Load-bearing for J3, idle for J1. Doubtful job: "we have no information bearing on which observers are simulated." Borrowed in part: the detailed defence is elsewhere (Synthese 2001, *Anthropic Bias*), and the paper says so. |
| P7 betting argument | Idle | It is P6 restated in stories. It rules out no rival. |
| P8 continuum argument | Held if | Weakly held: it does rule out step-shaped credence functions. A plausibility argument, not a test. |
| P9 convergence speculations | Loose | Offered as speculation, labelled as such. |
| P10 DOOM / not-special | Held, catch-all with a gauge | The gauge is named: a giant meteor would show we had been exceptionally unlucky. No gauge, no catch-all — this one has one. |
| P11 mildness vs theogony | Loose | Free in the harmless sense, and both are labelled. |

## 4. Whole-explanation checks

**Flip.** Swap P5 for "NI ≈ 1" and (3) stops following. This is not a story that fits any outcome — it moves when the world moves. The credence step (P6) has no flip test; it has a gauge instead. Good.

**Direction.** The paper keeps these apart: §IV is the forward question (what produces the observer count), §V the backward one (what should we think we are). This is exactly right and unusually careful.

**Answer hidden in the starting points?** P10 is close: conditional on Pf ≈ 0, DOOM follows by the meaning of (1). The paper says so rather than dressing it as a finding. Horn (2)'s "convergence" is flagged as unknown, not smuggled in.

**Pairs that pull.** The author names one: hoping (3) is true lowers the chance of (1), but if simulating posthumans is prohibitively expensive our simulators would switch us off before we got there — "then our best hope would be that (2) is true." Second: "the implications are not radical" against an afterlife and a universal ethical imperative. Both are labelled speculation, so both give way; nothing is hidden.

**Catch-alls.** Horn (2)'s "posthumans may be very different" is a bin. The only gauge offered is the derived claim that posthuman societies contain no free wealthy agents with human desires. Thin, and the paper says it is.

**Change list.** Rich and stated up front: errors of orders of magnitude, any time-scale, unknown physics, any motives. What it leaves out, it declares: consciousness itself, quantum-level universe simulation, selective and shadow-people simulations.

**Rivals.** (a) Credence should follow the prior chance of being simulated, not the count of observers. Nothing on this paper's list tells that apart from P6; the discriminating work is declared to be elsewhere. So **at this level, within this paper, they are the same explanation.** (b) Substrate-independence false — told apart by a named test: build a system replicating synaptic structure and see.

**Where the parts came from.** P1 asserted/borrowed; P2 fitted (conservative, so fitted on the safe side); P3–P5 built from the definitions; P6 borrowed, argued from analogy; P9, P11 labelled guesses.

## 5. What would make it harder to vary

1. Any observable difference between simulated and biological minds. That either holds P6 or breaks it, and it is the first real test the key step can meet.
2. An actual demonstration that a structurally replicated system is conscious — turning the largest borrowed part into a held one.

## 6. What this does not show

Hard to vary is not the same as true. The disjunction may hold while P6 stays borrowed; it may fail while the arithmetic is flawless.

## 7. One next step

Read the imported defence of the indifference principle (the Synthese 2001 paper) and run these tests on it, since within this paper it cannot be told from its rival.
